14:

18: 
19: ## 1. AT A GLANCE
20: 
21: | Aspect | What you get |
22: |---|---|
23: | **Use it for** | Real-app design references: screens for UI patterns and states, apps for category comparison, flows for step research, elements for component behavior in context, plus the Code Mode wiring state and auth expectations |

27: 
28: ---
29: 
30: ## 2. OVERVIEW
31: 
32: ### Why This Skill Exists
33: 
34: Mobbin holds one of the largest libraries of real app UI screenshots. It exposes that library through a paid hosted MCP. Live pre-auth discovery on 2026-07-16 listed exactly three read-only search tools, so an agent that guesses beyond them invents tools that do not exist. The auth model invites a worse guess: there is no API key, only browser OAuth, so a helper that wires a `MOBBIN_API_KEY` env var fabricates a credential path the provider never published. This README records the wiring truth, the three-tool contract, the auth expectations and the boundary that this transport produces no design tokens or Style Reference of its own: `sk-design-md-generator` is the measured-extraction companion for that.
35: 
36: ### What It Does
37: 
38: - **Transport**: This packet is a read-only TRANSPORT in the `mcp-tooling` hub (`packetKind: transport`, `mutatesWorkspace: false`). Every call happens against the external Mobbin service and nothing in this repo changes: the transport never changes a file and never dispatches another agent.
39: - **Wiring report**: It reports the `mobbin` manual's registration state honestly and carries the registered manual's reference shape.
40: - **Discovery first**: It mandates discovery-first callable confirmation before any call.
41: - **Research workflows**: Intent-shaped queries over `search_screens`, `limit` starting at 5, platform inferred or asked, every reference cited by `mobbin_url` and `failed[]` reported as partial success.
42: - **Companion**: Whenever a measured Style Reference of real, extracted design tokens is also wanted, `sk-design-md-generator` produces it from a live site. This transport supplies metadata and cited images, with every claim sourced from the provider response; its output is never a design-token set or Style Reference by itself.
43: 
44: ### When To Use This Skill
45: 
46: Reach for this packet when a user wants Mobbin evidence: real-app screens for a UI pattern or state, app-category comparison, flow research reconstructed from screens or element behavior in context. Reach for it too when the `mobbin` wiring state or its auth expectations need reporting. Skip it when the work is measured design-reference extraction (a live site's real CSS to a Style Reference DESIGN.md of named tokens), which belongs to `sk-design-md-generator` while this packet stays the transport. Skip it for Refero research (`mcp-refero`, the sibling transport), for Figma work (`mcp-figma`), for browser automation or previews (`mcp-chrome-devtools`) and for generic app coding (`sk-code`). Skip it for Mobbin's documentation search too: `docs.mobbin.com/mcp` is a separate docs-search MCP, not this packet's server. And never use it to change files: it is a read-only transport that never writes or edits files and never runs the Task tool. It never registers or edits the `.utcp_config.json` manual.
47: 
48: ### The Three-Tool Search Surface
49: 
50: Live pre-auth discovery confirmed a bounded read-only surface. Each tool covers one evidence domain. Every session re-confirms the callables with `tool_info` before the first call.
51: 
52: | Tool | What it searches | Notable inputs |
53: |---|---|---|
54: | `search_screens` | App and screen research, with element behavior in context | `query`, `platform` (ios or web), `mode` (deep, standard or fast), `limit`, `exclude_screen_ids`, `image_format` |
55: | `search_flows` | One user flow per query | `platform`, `limit`, `page` up to 20 |
56: | `search_sections` | One website section per query | `limit`, `page` |
57: 
58: ---
59: 
60: ## 3. QUICK START

62: > The examples below are illustrative. The `mobbin` manual is registered and the callables are discovery-confirmed (2026-07-16 fixture). Each session re-confirms them with `tool_info`. Live calls need an authenticated paid account (Pro or higher).

72: ```

75:

81: //   TS callables mobbin.mobbin_search_screens(...) etc.

Only the three tools above exist. Guessing beyond them means inventing tools the provider never shipped. The declared `search_screens` output is `{ query, screens[{id, app_name, mobbin_url, image_url, platform}] }`. The research-documented `index` and `failed[]` fields do not appear in the declared schema, so verify the actual shape on the first authenticated call. Full contract: [`references/tool-surface.md`](./references/tool-surface.md).
113: 
114: ### The Registered Wiring State
115: 
116: The provider is a hosted remote server over Streamable HTTP at `api.mobbin.com/mcp`. There is no local package. The official repo is registration metadata only. The local bridge is a `stdio` manual that launches `npx -y mcp-remote https://api.mobbin.com/mcp` with an empty env, drafted byte-identically by two research lineages and now registered in `.utcp_config.json` (2026-07-16, operator-applied verbatim, reference shape in [`assets/utcp-mobbin-manual.md`](./assets/utcp-mobbin-manual.md)). Per-session `tool_info` re-confirmation before first use stays the rule.
117: 
118: ### Authentication Without An API Key
119: 
120: Mobbin MCP auth is browser OAuth only: protected-resource discovery, Dynamic Client Registration (RFC 7591), authorization code with PKCE S256 and the `openid` scope, revocable from Account Settings. A live unauthenticated probe returned HTTP 401 with a `WWW-Authenticate` pointer to the protected-resource metadata. That challenge is the expected shape, not a missing-key error. Adapter auth state under `~/.mcp-auth` is operator-owned. End-to-end OAuth through the local bridge is Inferred, not verified.
121: 
122: ### Plans And Limits
123: 
124: Plan gating is hard: MCP access starts at Pro or higher. Free has no MCP access. The service enforces 60 requests per 60 seconds per user. On HTTP 429, honor `Retry-After` and back off with jitter.
125: 
126: ### The Transport Boundary
127: 
128: The transport allows breadth while researching: apps, screens, flows and intents compared through metadata and images. But it produces no design tokens or Style Reference of its own. A transport response is untrusted reference evidence.
129: 
130: - A measured Style Reference of real, extracted design tokens is `sk-design-md-generator`'s output, not the transport's.
131: - That companion skill measures a live website's real CSS into named tokens, a type scale, components and Quick-Start CSS/Tailwind.
132: - Search rank is not a verdict. An appealing screenshot is not a measured token.
133: - Evidence is cited and never copied wholesale.

14: # Skill README Template
15: 
16: Use this template for `.skilled/skills/[skill-name]/README.md`. It writes a skill README in the same narrative voice the repo root `README.md` and the changelogs use: a one-line human pitch, an at-a-glance table near the top, a value-first overview, then quick start, navigation and a verification close.
17: 
18: ---
19: 
20: ## 1. OVERVIEW
21: 
22: ### Purpose
23: 
24: Give a person a fast, honest orientation to a skill before they open `SKILL.md`. The README answers what outcome the skill delivers, when to reach for it, what it does not own and how to navigate its files. `SKILL.md` stays the runtime instruction surface. The README is the front door a person reads.
25: 
26: ### Identity Guidance (Purpose First)
27: 
28: The identity of a skill is the outcome it delivers. State that outcome in one plain sentence before naming tools.
29: Describe CLIs, commands, routing paths and reference files only after the outcome.
30: A README that opens with a tool name has not stated its identity.
31: 
32: The mcp-obsidian README states the outcome first: it makes AI use inside Obsidian effective.
33: It names the CLIs and MCP server later as delivery surfaces.
34: Repeat the outcome in the frontmatter description and the pitch.
35: The description supports a quick scan. The pitch opens the full README.
36: 
37: ### Usage
38: 
39: Copy the fillable scaffold in Section 6 into `.skilled/skills/[skill-name]/README.md`, then replace every placeholder with current behavior taken from the skill's real files. Keep the numbered ALL-CAPS section headers, the house style and the validator both require them. Drop any section that does not earn its place and renumber the rest.
40: 
41: ### Template Focus
42: 
43: The README gives people a human entry point, current capabilities and a clear route to supporting files. This template provides:
44: 
45: - A one-line pitch in a blockquote right after the H1, stating the outcome before any tool name.
46: - An identity guidance block that puts the delivered outcome ahead of the tooling.
47: - A capability section pattern for a skill's headline strengths, modeled on the pilot's Plugin Knowledge Layer.
48: - A dedicated HVR enforcement section with the banned forms and the scripted checks.
49: - Versioning conventions and a validation checklist that matches the pilot's gates.
50: 
51: ---
52: 
53: ## 2. SECTION MODEL
54: 
55: A skill README uses numbered ALL-CAPS H2 sections with `---` dividers between them. The default order:
56: 
57: | # | Section | Purpose | Keep When |
58: |---|---------|---------|-----------|
59: | 1 | AT A GLANCE | Four-row table a reader scans in five seconds | Always |
60: | 2 | OVERVIEW | What the skill is and what the reader gets first, then the optional problem narrative | Always (required by the validator) |
61: | 3 | QUICK START | The fastest path to a first result | Skill has commands, scripts or a workflow |
62: | 4 | HOW IT WORKS | The main workflow in prose, with a small Mermaid diagram for multi-step flows | Skill has non-obvious behavior worth explaining |
63: | 5 | INTEGRATION & NAVIGATION | When to use it, plus how it hands off to sibling skills | Readers can confuse it with a neighbor |
64: | 6 | TROUBLESHOOTING | The failure modes operators actually hit | Predictable issues exist |
65: | 7 | FAQ | The two to five questions readers keep asking | High-value answers exist |
66: | 8 | VERIFICATION | How you know the skill works | Skill ships a playbook or validation command |
67: | 9 | RELATED DOCUMENTS | Stable links out, `SKILL.md` first | Always when links exist |
68: 
69: `OVERVIEW` is the one required section. Its normalized name must appear as a numbered header so the validator finds it. Every other section is optional. A small utility skill might run four sections (AT A GLANCE, OVERVIEW, QUICK START, RELATED DOCUMENTS). A large orchestrator might run all nine. Match the count to the skill. Never pad to hit a number.
70: 
71: Inside OVERVIEW, start with `### What It Does`. Say what the skill is and what the reader gets.
72: Add up to two optional subsections after it.
73: Use `### Why This Skill Exists` only to name a current reader problem.
74: Add the capability section below when it earns a table.
75: 
76: ### Capability Section Pattern
77: 
78: When a skill has a headline strength, add a named capability section after What It Does.
79: Use one or two short sentences to say why the strength matters.
80: Use an analogy only when it clarifies the mechanism.
81: Name the section after its domain and add one table row per capability.
82: State the file or data the skill can operate on.
83: Avoid marketing claims. The prose explains why the capability matters. The table states what it does.
84: 
85: ```markdown
86: ### The Plugin Knowledge Layer
87: 
88: | Plugin | What the skill knows how to operate |
89: |---|---|
90: | **Beancount Ledger** | append and patch balanced transactions in the structured `.beancount` ledger |
91: | **Obsidian Tables** | edit `columns`, `rows` and `views` inside `.table.md` JSON payloads |
92: ```
93: 
94: ---
95: 
96: ## 3. WRITING RULES
97: 
98: - Apply the [Prose Clarity Checklist](../../references/skill/creation-workflow.md#prose-clarity-checklist) to README prose.
99: - State the outcome before the tooling. The pitch and the identity guidance name what the reader gets. The tool names follow as the means.
100: - Open OVERVIEW with what the skill is and what the reader gets.
101: - Use `### Why This Skill Exists` only to explain a current reader problem.
102: - Add a short context hook after the blockquote only when it helps the reader. Keep AT A GLANCE as the first numbered section.
103: - Carry the explanation in prose. Reach for a table only when 4 or more parallel items need a lookup grid (skill relationships, CLI flags, a comparison).
104: - Use semantic emoji only (✅ ❌ ⚠️ 🔒 🚨) for rules and status markers. Decorative section emoji never: that register belongs to the repository front-page README, while a skill README keeps the technical formatting.
105: - A short, concrete analogy can carry an abstract mechanism better than adjectives (the repo root README uses "like a lab notebook for software"). Use one only where it clarifies, never as decoration.
106: - Put the AT A GLANCE table first. Four rows, one line each, no prose cells.
107: - Name the canonical command or entry point in OVERVIEW or QUICK START so a reader knows where to start.
108: - Link to real files under `references/`, `assets/`, `scripts/`, `feature-catalog/` or `manual-testing-playbook/`. Verify each path resolves.
109: - State the expected output for every command you show, so a reader can tell success from failure.
110: - Be honest about boundaries and trade-offs. If the skill does not own something, say which skill does.
111: - Keep `SKILL.md` as the runtime surface. The README explains why and how to navigate. It does not restate long reference files.
112: - Follow the Human Voice Rules. Section 4 lists the banned forms and the scripted checks. It links the full ruleset.
113: - Vary subsection counts rather than defaulting to three.
114: - Document current behavior. Keep spec history out of the README.
115: - Use stable paths and commands. Update the README, its version and its changelog entry when behavior changes.
116: 
117: ---
118: 
119: ## 4. HVR ENFORCEMENT
120: 
121: Every README this template produces must pass the Human Voice Rules. The full ruleset lives at [`hvr-rules.md`](../../../sk-create-with-human-voice/references/hvr-rules.md).
122: 
123: ### Banned Forms
124: 
125: The banned forms are: em dashes (U+2014), semicolons (U+003B), Oxford commas (a comma before the final and or or in a list), the hard-blocker words listed below and forced three-item groups.
126: 
127: ### Scripted Checks
128: 
129: Run the checks below from the skill root, with the README path as the argument. Each command must return zero matches. The punctuation checks use hex escapes on purpose: the commands stay clean of the characters they enforce.
130: 
131: ```bash
132: rg -n '\x{2014}' README.md
133: rg -n '\x{3B}' README.md
134: rg -n ',\s+(and|or)\b' README.md
135: rg -n '\b(delve|embark|realm|tapestry|illuminate|unveil|elucidate|abyss|revolutionise|game-changer|groundbreaking|cutting-edge|ever-evolving|shed light|dive deep|leverage|foster|nurture|resonate|empower|disrupt|curate|harness|elevate|robust|seamless|holistic|synergy|unpack|landscape|ecosystem|journey|paradigm|enlightening|esteemed|remarkable|skyrocket|skyrocketing|utilize|utilizing)\b' README.md
136: # Context-dependent words: landscape, ecosystem, journey, unlock, navigating
137: # Banned as metaphor, allowed in literal use. Judge each hit in context.
138: ```
139: 
140: The word check lists the hard blockers. A hit inside a code sample or a quoted command is exempt. A hit in prose is a violation. Context-dependent words from the full ruleset are banned as metaphor and allowed in literal use. Judge each hit in context.
141: 
142: Forced three-item groups are the fifth banned form. No exactly-three inline enumerations: use 2, 4 or 5 items. Tables and bullet lists are exempt. No exactly-three H3 subsections under every H2: vary the count.
143: 
144: ---
145: 
146: ## 5. VERSIONING CONVENTIONS
147: 
148: Every skill README carries a version in its frontmatter: `version: X.Y.Z.W`, the same 4-part scheme `SKILL.md` uses. Bump the README version on every release, whether the change touched the README text or the skill it documents. The README states the current state, so a behavior change is a README change even when the prose barely moves.
149: 
150: Every release gets a per-skill changelog entry at `changelog/<version>.md`. The entry follows the shared [changelog template](../../../sk-create-changelog/assets/changelog-template.md) and its message-release shape: NEW covers what arrived, CHANGED covers what moved, NOT CHANGED covers what stayed untouched.
151: 
152: `SKILL.md` and the README carry versions that move together. A skill release bumps both files. The changelog entry records the new version.
153: 
154: ---
155: 
156: ## 6. FILLABLE SCAFFOLD
157: 
158: Copy this into `.skilled/skills/[skill-name]/README.md`, fill every placeholder from the skill's real files, then remove sections that do not fit and renumber.
159:

162: title: "[skill-name]"
163: description: "[One sentence. The outcome the skill delivers, stated before any tool name, then who reaches for it.]"
164: trigger_phrases:

173: 
174: [Optional. Add one or two sentences about the reader's current need before the scan table. Delete this for a small utility skill. AT A GLANCE stays the first numbered section.]
175: 
176: ---
177: 
178: ## 1. AT A GLANCE
179: 
180: | Aspect | What you get |
181: |---|---|
182: | **Use it for** | [The problem it solves, one line.] |

It writes a skill README in the same narrative voice the repo root `README.md` and the changelogs use: a one-line human pitch, an at-a-glance table near the top, a value-first overview, then quick start, navigation and a verification close.
17: 
18: ---
19: 
20: ## 1. OVERVIEW
21: 
22: ### Purpose
23: 
24: Give a person a fast, honest orientation to a skill before they open `SKILL.md`. The README answers what outcome the skill delivers, when to reach for it, what it does not own and how to navigate its files. `SKILL.md` stays the runtime instruction surface. The README is the front door a person reads.
25: 
26: ### Identity Guidance (Purpose First)
27: 
28: The identity of a skill is the outcome it delivers. State that outcome in one plain sentence before naming tools.
29: Describe CLIs, commands, routing paths and reference files only after the outcome.
30: A README that opens with a tool name has not stated its identity.
31: 
32: The mcp-obsidian README states the outcome first: it makes AI use inside Obsidian effective.
33: It names the CLIs and MCP server later as delivery surfaces.
34: Repeat the outcome in the frontmatter description and the pitch.
35: The description supports a quick scan. The pitch opens the full README.
36: 
37: ### Usage
38: 
39: Copy the fillable scaffold in Section 6 into `.skilled/skills/[skill-name]/README.md`, then replace every placeholder with current behavior taken from the skill's real files. Keep the numbered ALL-CAPS section headers, the house style and the validator both require them. Drop any section that does not earn its place and renumber the rest.
40: 
41: ### Template Focus
42: 
43: The README gives people a human entry point, current capabilities and a clear route to supporting files. This template provides:
44: 
45: - A one-line pitch in a blockquote right after the H1, stating the outcome before any tool name.
46: - An identity guidance block that puts the delivered outcome ahead of the tooling.
47: - A capability section pattern for a skill's headline strengths, modeled on the pilot's Plugin Knowledge Layer.
48: - A dedicated HVR enforcement section with the banned forms and the scripted checks.
49: - Versioning conventions and a validation checklist that matches the pilot's gates.
50: 
51: ---
52: 
53: ## 2. SECTION MODEL
54: 
55: A skill README uses numbered ALL-CAPS H2 sections with `---` dividers between them. The default order:
56: 
57: | # | Section | Purpose | Keep When |
58: |---|---------|---------|-----------|
59: | 1 | AT A GLANCE | Four-row table a reader scans in five seconds | Always |
60: | 2 | OVERVIEW | What the skill is and what the reader gets first, then the optional problem narrative | Always (required by the validator) |
61: | 3 | QUICK START | The fastest path to a first result | Skill has commands, scripts or a workflow |
62: | 4 | HOW IT WORKS | The main workflow in prose, with a small Mermaid diagram for multi-step flows | Skill has non-obvious behavior worth explaining |
63: | 5 | INTEGRATION & NAVIGATION | When to use it, plus how it hands off to sibling skills | Readers can confuse it with a neighbor |
64: | 6 | TROUBLESHOOTING | The failure modes operators actually hit | Predictable issues exist |
65: | 7 | FAQ | The two to five questions readers keep asking | High-value answers exist |
66: | 8 | VERIFICATION | How you know the skill works | Skill ships a playbook or validation command |
67: | 9 | RELATED DOCUMENTS | Stable links out, `SKILL.md` first | Always when links exist |
68: 
69: `OVERVIEW` is the one required section. Its normalized name must appear as a numbered header so the validator finds it. Every other section is optional. A small utility skill might run four sections (AT A GLANCE, OVERVIEW, QUICK START, RELATED DOCUMENTS). A large orchestrator might run all nine. Match the count to the skill. Never pad to hit a number.
70: 
71: Inside OVERVIEW, start with `### What It Does`. Say what the skill is and what the reader gets.
72: Add up to two optional subsections after it.
73: Use `### Why This Skill Exists` only to name a current reader problem.
74: Add the capability section below when it earns a table.
75: 
76: ### Capability Section Pattern
77: 
78: When a skill has a headline strength, add a named capability section after What It Does.
79: Use one or two short sentences to say why the strength matters.
80: Use an analogy only when it clarifies the mechanism.
81: Name the section after its domain and add one table row per capability.
82: State the file or data the skill can operate on.
83: Avoid marketing claims. The prose explains why the capability matters. The table states what it does.

87: 
88: | Plugin | What the skill knows how to operate |
89: |---|---|
90: | **Beancount Ledger** | append and patch balanced transactions in the structured `.beancount` ledger |
91: | **Obsidian Tables** | edit `columns`, `rows` and `views` inside `.table.md` JSON payloads |
92: ```

96: ## 3. WRITING RULES
97: 
98: - Apply the [Prose Clarity Checklist](../../references/skill/creation-workflow.md#prose-clarity-checklist) to README prose.
99: - State the outcome before the tooling. The pitch and the identity guidance name what the reader gets. The tool names follow as the means.
100: - Open OVERVIEW with what the skill is and what the reader gets.
101: - Use `### Why This Skill Exists` only to explain a current reader problem.
102: - Add a short context hook after the blockquote only when it helps the reader. Keep AT A GLANCE as the first numbered section.
103: - Carry the explanation in prose. Reach for a table only when 4 or more parallel items need a lookup grid (skill relationships, CLI flags, a comparison).
104: - Use semantic emoji only (✅ ❌ ⚠️ 🔒 🚨) for rules and status markers. Decorative section emoji never: that register belongs to the repository front-page README, while a skill README keeps the technical formatting.
105: - A short, concrete analogy can carry an abstract mechanism better than adjectives (the repo root README uses "like a lab notebook for software"). Use one only where it clarifies, never as decoration.
106: - Put the AT A GLANCE table first. Four rows, one line each, no prose cells.
107: - Name the canonical command or entry point in OVERVIEW or QUICK START so a reader knows where to start.
108: - Link to real files under `references/`, `assets/`, `scripts/`, `feature-catalog/` or `manual-testing-playbook/`. Verify each path resolves.
109: - State the expected output for every command you show, so a reader can tell success from failure.
110: - Be honest about boundaries and trade-offs. If the skill does not own something, say which skill does.
111: - Keep `SKILL.md` as the runtime surface. The README explains why and how to navigate. It does not restate long reference files.
112: - Follow the Human Voice Rules. Section 4 lists the banned forms and the scripted checks. It links the full ruleset.
113: - Vary subsection counts rather than defaulting to three.
114: - Document current behavior. Keep spec history out of the README.
115: - Use stable paths and commands. Update the README, its version and its changelog entry when behavior changes.

119: ## 4. HVR ENFORCEMENT
120: 
121: Every README this template produces must pass the Human Voice Rules. The full ruleset lives at [`hvr-rules.md`](../../../sk-create-with-human-voice/references/hvr-rules.md).
122: 
123: ### Banned Forms
124: 
125: The banned forms are: em dashes (U+2014), semicolons (U+003B), Oxford commas (a comma before the final and or or in a list), the hard-blocker words listed below and forced three-item groups.
126: 
127: ### Scripted Checks
128: 
129: Run the checks below from the skill root, with the README path as the argument. Each command must return zero matches. The punctuation checks use hex escapes on purpose: the commands stay clean of the characters they enforce.
130: 
131: ```bash
132: rg -n '\x{2014}' README.md
133: rg -n '\x{3B}' README.md
134: rg -n ',\s+(and|or)\b' README.md
135: rg -n '\b(delve|embark|realm|tapestry|illuminate|unveil|elucidate|abyss|revolutionise|game-changer|groundbreaking|cutting-edge|ever-evolving|shed light|dive deep|leverage|foster|nurture|resonate|empower|disrupt|curate|harness|elevate|robust|seamless|holistic|synergy|unpack|landscape|ecosystem|journey|paradigm|enlightening|esteemed|remarkable|skyrocket|skyrocketing|utilize|utilizing)\b' README.md
136: # Context-dependent words: landscape, ecosystem, journey, unlock, navigating
137: # Banned as metaphor, allowed in literal use. Judge each hit in context.
138: ```
139: 
140: The word check lists the hard blockers. A hit inside a code sample or a quoted command is exempt. A hit in prose is a violation. Context-dependent words from the full ruleset are banned as metaphor and allowed in literal use. Judge each hit in context.
141: 
142: Forced three-item groups are the fifth banned form. No exactly-three inline enumerations: use 2, 4 or 5 items. Tables and bullet lists are exempt. No exactly-three H3 subsections under every H2: vary the count.

---

## 2. OVERVIEW

### Why This Skill Exists

Mobbin holds one of the largest libraries of real app UI screenshots. It exposes that library through a paid hosted MCP. Reaching it from a coding agent without a written contract is risky in specific, documented ways. Live pre-auth discovery on 2026-07-16 listed exactly three read-only search tools, so an agent that guesses beyond them invents tools that do not exist. The auth model invites a worse guess: there is no API key, only browser OAuth, so a helper that wires a `MOBBIN_API_KEY` env var fabricates a credential path the provider never published. This README records the wiring truth, the three-tool contract, the auth expectations and the boundary that this transport produces no design tokens or Style Reference of its own: `sk-design-md-generator` is the measured-extraction companion for that.

### What It Does

This packet is a read-only TRANSPORT in the `mcp-tooling` hub (`packetKind: transport`, `mutatesWorkspace: false`). It reports the `mobbin` manual's registration state honestly, carries the registered manual's reference shape, mandates discovery-first callable confirmation before any call and runs the research workflows: intent-shaped queries over `search_screens`, `limit` starting at 5, platform inferred or asked, every reference cited by `mobbin_url` and `failed[]` reported as partial success. Every call happens against the external Mobbin service and nothing in this repo changes: the transport is read-only, never changes a file and never dispatches another agent. Whenever a measured Style Reference of real, extracted design tokens is also wanted, `sk-design-md-generator` produces it from a live site. This transport supplies metadata and cited images, with every claim sourced from the provider response; its output is never a design-token set or Style Reference by itself.

### The Three-Tool Search Surface

Live pre-auth discovery confirmed a bounded read-only surface. Each tool covers one evidence domain. Every session re-confirms the callables with `tool_info` before the first call.

| Tool | What it searches | Notable inputs |
|---|---|---|
| `search_screens` | App and screen research, with element behavior in context | `query`, `platform` (ios or web), `mode` (deep, standard or fast), `limit`, `exclude_screen_ids`, `image_format` |
| `search_flows` | One user flow per query | `platform`, `limit`, `page` up to 20 |
| `search_sections` | One website section per query | `limit`, `page` |

---

## 3. QUICK START

> The examples below are illustrative. The `mobbin` manual is registered and the callables are discovery-confirmed (2026-07-16 fixture). Each session re-confirms them with `tool_info`. Live calls need an authenticated paid account (Pro or higher).

**Step 1: Check the wiring state (read-only).**

```bash
bash .skilled/skills/mcp-tooling/mcp-mobbin/scripts/doctor.sh
# Confirms node/npx and reports the 'mobbin' manual state in .utcp_config.json (grep only,
=== 100-150 ===
## 4. HOW IT WORKS

### The Live Three-Tool Surface

Live pre-auth discovery on 2026-07-16 ([`references/discovery-fixture-2026-07-16.json`](./references/discovery-fixture-2026-07-16.json)) supersedes the earlier one-public-tool baseline. The registry lists three read-only search tools. The `deep` dispute is resolved: it is a client-settable `mode` input on `search_screens`, where `"deep"` selects the AI-powered relevance pipeline. App and screen research remain query intents over `search_screens`. Element research is another query intent on the same tool. Flows and website sections have their own tools. Only the three tools above exist. Guessing beyond them means inventing tools the provider never shipped. The declared `search_screens` output is `{ query, screens[{id, app_name, mobbin_url, image_url, platform}] }`. The research-documented `index` and `failed[]` fields do not appear in the declared schema, so verify the actual shape on the first authenticated call. Full contract: [`references/tool-surface.md`](./references/tool-surface.md).

### The Registered Wiring State

The provider is a hosted remote server over Streamable HTTP at `api.mobbin.com/mcp`. There is no local package. The official repo is registration metadata only. The local bridge is a `stdio` manual that launches `npx -y mcp-remote https://api.mobbin.com/mcp` with an empty env, drafted byte-identically by two research lineages and now registered in `.utcp_config.json` (2026-07-16, operator-applied verbatim, reference shape in [`assets/utcp-mobbin-manual.md`](./assets/utcp-mobbin-manual.md)). Live discovery ran the same day, pre-auth: the Code Mode callable `mobbin.mobbin_search_screens(...)` is confirmed (registry name `mobbin.mobbin.search_screens`, fixture [`references/discovery-fixture-2026-07-16.json`](./references/discovery-fixture-2026-07-16.json)) and two additional tools were listed. Per-session `tool_info` re-confirmation before first use stays the rule.

### Authentication Without An API Key

Mobbin MCP auth is browser OAuth only: protected-resource discovery, Dynamic Client Registration (RFC 7591), authorization code with PKCE S256 and the `openid` scope, revocable from Account Settings. A live unauthenticated probe returned HTTP 401 with a `WWW-Authenticate` pointer to the protected-resource metadata. That challenge is the expected shape, not a missing-key error. No static API key exists for MCP. The API-key Bearer model belongs to the separate Team and Enterprise REST API, so the manual `env` stays empty and no `.env` line is ever added. Adapter auth state under `~/.mcp-auth` is operator-owned. End-to-end OAuth through the local bridge is Inferred, not verified. Plan gating is hard: MCP access starts at Pro or higher. Free has no MCP access. The service enforces 60 requests per 60 seconds per user. On HTTP 429, honor `Retry-After` and back off with jitter.

### The Transport Boundary

The transport allows breadth while researching: apps, screens, flows and intents compared through metadata and images. But it produces no design tokens or Style Reference of its own. A transport response is untrusted reference evidence.

- A measured Style Reference of real, extracted design tokens is `sk-design-md-generator`'s output, not the transport's.
- That companion skill measures a live website's real CSS into named tokens, a type scale, components and Quick-Start CSS/Tailwind.
- Search rank is not a verdict. An appealing screenshot is not a measured token.
- Evidence is cited and never copied wholesale.

---

## 5. INTEGRATION & NAVIGATION

### When To Use This Skill

Reach for this packet when a user wants Mobbin evidence: real-app screens for a UI pattern or state, app-category comparison, flow research reconstructed from screens or element behavior in context. Reach for it too when the `mobbin` wiring state or its auth expectations need reporting. Skip it when the work is measured design-reference extraction (a live site's real CSS to a Style Reference DESIGN.md of named tokens), which belongs to `sk-design-md-generator` while this packet stays the transport. Skip it for Refero research (`mcp-refero`, the sibling transport), for Figma work (`mcp-figma`), for browser automation or previews (`mcp-chrome-devtools`) and for generic app coding (`sk-code`). Skip it for Mobbin's documentation search too: `docs.mobbin.com/mcp` is a separate docs-search MCP, not this packet's server. And never use it to change files: it is a read-only transport that never writes or edits files and never runs the Task tool. It never registers or edits the `.utcp_config.json` manual.

### Related Skills

The packet is the hub's third transport. Its closest structural sibling is `mcp-refero`: both are remote-MCP-via-`mcp-remote`, read-only, OAuth-gated design-research transports with no CLI machinery. What separates this packet from Refero is the three-tool surface and the no-API-key auth model.

| Skill | Relationship |
|---|---|
| `sk-design-md-generator` | The measured-extraction companion. It turns a live website's real CSS into a Style Reference DESIGN.md of named design tokens. This packet retrieves Mobbin screenshot evidence; that skill produces the measured Style Reference |
| `mcp-code-mode` | The substrate. Manuals, `{manual}.{manual}_{tool}` naming, discovery and error-envelope discipline all come from Code Mode |
| `mcp-refero` | The closest sibling: another remote-MCP-via-`mcp-remote`, read-only, OAuth-gated design-research transport. Refero covers styles, screens and flows with 8 tools. Mobbin covers screens, flows and sections with 3 |
| `mcp-figma` | The hub's original Figma transport (CLI-primary with optional MCP). No surface overlap with Mobbin |
| `mcp-chrome-devtools` | Browser inspection and preview, never a design-reference search surface |
| `sk-code` | Owns adapting any resulting design decision into application code and verifying it |

---

This README records the wiring truth, the three-tool contract, the auth expectations and the boundary that this transport produces no design tokens or Style Reference of its own: `sk-design-md-generator` is the measured-extraction companion for that.

### What It Does

This packet is a read-only TRANSPORT in the `mcp-tooling` hub (`packetKind: transport`, `mutatesWorkspace: false`). It reports the `mobbin` manual's registration state honestly, carries the registered manual's reference shape, mandates discovery-first callable confirmation before any call and runs the research workflows: intent-shaped queries over `search_screens`, `limit` starting at 5, platform inferred or asked, every reference cited by `mobbin_url` and `failed[]` reported as partial success. Every call happens against the external Mobbin service and nothing in this repo changes: the transport is read-only, never changes a file and never dispatches another agent. Whenever a measured Style Reference of real, extracted design tokens is also wanted, `sk-design-md-generator` produces it from a live site. This transport supplies metadata and cited images, with every claim sourced from the provider response; its output is never a design-token set or Style Reference by itself.

### The Three-Tool Search Surface

Live pre-auth discovery confirmed a bounded read-only surface. Each tool covers one evidence domain. Every session re-confirms the callables with `tool_info` before the first call.

| Tool | What it searches | Notable inputs |
|---|---|---|
| `search_screens` | App and screen research, with element behavior in context | `query`, `platform` (ios or web), `mode` (deep, standard or fast), `limit`, `exclude_screen_ids`, `image_format` |
| `search_flows` | One user flow per query | `platform`, `limit`, `page` up to 20 |
| `search_sections` | One website section per query | `limit`, `page` |

## 4. HOW IT WORKS

### The Live Three-Tool Surface

Live pre-auth discovery on 2026-07-16 ([`references/discovery-fixture-2026-07-16.json`](./references/discovery-fixture-2026-07-16.json)) supersedes the earlier one-public-tool baseline. The registry lists three read-only search tools. The `deep` dispute is resolved: it is a client-settable `mode` input on `search_screens`, where `"deep"` selects the AI-powered relevance pipeline. App and screen research remain query intents over `search_screens`. Element research is another query intent on the same tool. Flows and website sections have their own tools. Only the three tools above exist. Guessing beyond them means inventing tools the provider never shipped. The declared `search_screens` output is `{ query, screens[{id, app_name, mobbin_url, image_url, platform}] }`. The research-documented `index` and `failed[]` fields do not appear in the declared schema, so verify the actual shape on the first authenticated call. Full contract: [`references/tool-surface.md`](./references/tool-surface.md).

### The Registered Wiring State

The provider is a hosted remote server over Streamable HTTP at `api.mobbin.com/mcp`. There is no local package. The official repo is registration metadata only. The local bridge is a `stdio` manual that launches `npx -y mcp-remote https://api.mobbin.com/mcp` with an empty env, drafted byte-identically by two research lineages and now registered in `.utcp_config.json` (2026-07-16, operator-applied verbatim, reference shape in [`assets/utcp-mobbin-manual.md`](./assets/utcp-mobbin-manual.md)). Live discovery ran the same day, pre-auth: the Code Mode callable `mobbin.mobbin_search_screens(...)` is confirmed (registry name `mobbin.mobbin.search_screens`, fixture [`references/discovery-fixture-2026-07-16.json`](./references/discovery-fixture-2026-07-16.json)) and two additional tools were listed. Per-session `tool_info` re-confirmation before first use stays the rule.

### Authentication Without An API Key

Mobbin MCP auth is browser OAuth only: protected-resource discovery, Dynamic Client Registration (RFC 7591), authorization code with PKCE S256 and the `openid` scope, revocable from Account Settings. A live unauthenticated probe returned HTTP 401 with a `WWW-Authenticate` pointer to the protected-resource metadata. That challenge is the expected shape, not a missing-key error. No static API key exists for MCP. The API-key Bearer model belongs to the separate Team and Enterprise REST API, so the manual `env` stays empty and no `.env` line is ever added. Adapter auth state under `~/.mcp-auth` is operator-owned. End-to-end OAuth through the local bridge is Inferred, not verified. Plan gating is hard: MCP access starts at Pro or higher. Free has no MCP access. The service enforces 60 requests per 60 seconds per user. On HTTP 429, honor `Retry-After` and back off with jitter.

### The Transport Boundary

The transport allows breadth while researching: apps, screens, flows and intents compared through metadata and images. But it produces no design tokens or Style Reference of its own. A transport response is untrusted reference evidence.

- A measured Style Reference of real, extracted design tokens is `sk-design-md-generator`'s output, not the transport's.
- That companion skill measures a live website's real CSS into named tokens, a type scale, components and Quick-Start CSS/Tailwind.
- Search rank is not a verdict. An appealing screenshot is not a measured token.
- Evidence is cited and never copied wholesale.

---

## 5. INTEGRATION & NAVIGATION

### When To Use This Skill

Reach for this packet when a user wants Mobbin evidence: real-app screens for a UI pattern or state, app-category comparison, flow research reconstructed from screens or element behavior in context. Reach for it too when the `mobbin` wiring state or its auth expectations need reporting. Skip it when the work is measured design-reference extraction (a live site's real CSS to a Style Reference DESIGN.md of named tokens), which belongs to `sk-design-md-generator` while this packet stays the transport. Skip it for Refero research (`mcp-refero`, the sibling transport), for Figma work (`mcp-figma`), for browser automation or previews (`mcp-chrome-devtools`) and for generic app coding (`sk-code`). Skip it for Mobbin's documentation search too: `docs.mobbin.com/mcp` is a separate docs-search MCP, not this packet's server. And never use it to change files: it is a read-only transport that never writes or edits files and never runs the Task tool. It never registers or edits the `.utcp_config.json` manual.

### Related Skills

The packet is the hub's third transport. Its closest structural sibling is `mcp-refero`: both are remote-MCP-via-`mcp-remote`, read-only, OAuth-gated design-research transports with no CLI machinery. What separates this packet from Refero is the three-tool surface and the no-API-key auth model.

Unauthenticated calls return HTTP 401. The service is rate-limited to **60 requests per 60 seconds per user**.

28: ## 1. WHEN TO USE
29: 
30: ### Activation Triggers
31: 
32: **Use when** the user wants to:
33: - Search Mobbin for real-app design references: screens for a UI pattern or state, apps for category comparison, flows for journey steps, or elements for component behavior in context.
34: - Find screen examples from shipped apps ("show me iOS banking onboarding screens", "web empty-state dashboard examples").
35: - Research how real products handle a flow or journey through screen evidence ("first-run onboarding progression", "forgot-password recovery").
36: - Wire, verify, or troubleshoot the registered `mobbin` Code Mode manual, its OAuth authentication, its plan gating, or its rate limit.
37: 
38: **Keyword Triggers**: "mobbin", "mobbin mcp", "app design research", "screen examples", "ux flow references", "real app screenshots", "search mobbin".
39: 
40: ### Use Cases
41: 
42: **App research (read-only).** Name the app, company, or category plus the comparison goal ("banking apps onboarding identity verification"); compare `app_name`, platform, structure, and visible patterns across results. Multiple results are evidence, not a design chooser.
43: 
44: **Screen research (read-only).** Name the concrete screen, state, or job ("iOS subscription cancellation confirmation"); start at 5 results; cite each `mobbin_url` used.
45: 
46: **Flow research (read-only).** Describe the journey and target step. The public contract returns screens, not an ordered flow object — reconstruct sequence only when visual evidence supports it, and label the reconstruction as inference.
47: 
48: **Element research (read-only).** Name component plus context/state ("bottom-sheet destructive confirmation", "inline validation on signup"); analyze element behavior within returned screens.
49: 
50: **Wiring and auth verification.** Report the manual's registration state honestly (presence is the healthy result; absence is a failure symptom to escalate), explain the OAuth-only model and plan gate, and never repair auth state yourself.

52: ### When NOT to Use
53: 
54: **Skip this skill when:**
55: - The work is measured design-reference extraction: turning a live website's real CSS into a Style Reference DESIGN.md of named design tokens (type scale, components, Quick-Start CSS/Tailwind). That is `sk-design-md-generator`; this packet only retrieves Mobbin screenshot evidence.
56: - The task is styles, screens, or flows research through Refero. That is `mcp-refero`, the sibling transport.
57: - The task is Figma work (inspect, tokens, render, Code Connect). That is `mcp-figma`.
58: - The task is browser automation, live-page inspection, or visual preview of a built page. That is `mcp-chrome-devtools`.
59: - The work is generic app coding with no design-reference input: use `sk-code`.
60: - The target is Mobbin's documentation search. `docs.mobbin.com/mcp` is a **separate** Mintlify docs-search MCP, not the design-reference server; this packet targets `api.mobbin.com/mcp` only.
61: - The user asks to change this repo's files, edit the registered `.utcp_config.json` manual, or repair auth state. This transport forbids Write/Edit/Task, never mutates the workspace, and the registered manual is operator-owned.

78: ## 3. HOW IT WORKS
79:

88: //   mobbin.mobbin.search_screens · mobbin.mobbin.search_flows · mobbin.mobbin.search_sections
89: const all = await list_tools();
90: // MANDATORY per session: confirm the exact callable + schema before relying on any name
91: const info = await tool_info({ tool_name: "mobbin.mobbin_search_screens" });

94: Live discovery on 2026-07-16 **CONFIRMED both the dotted discovery names and the callable form** (`references/discovery-fixture-2026-07-16.json`). The convention-derived prediction held exactly.

99: 
100: The research's **one publicly documented tool** baseline is superseded: live pre-auth discovery on 2026-07-16 listed **three** read-only search tools. All three passed the mutation-refusal check (no mutation-capable tool in the listing). Full fixture schemas and the completeness boundary: [`references/tool-surface.md`](references/tool-surface.md).

105: | `search_flows` | Read/search | `query` (one journey); `platform` `"ios"`\|`"web"` | `limit`; `page` (max 20); `image_format` |

111: Never invent `search_apps`, `search_elements` or any detail, image-download or mutation tool beyond the discovered inventory.

113: ### Calling through Code Mode
114: 
115: > **Callable-name status.** Live discovery on 2026-07-16 confirmed the callable form (`references/discovery-fixture-2026-07-16.json`). The registry name is `mobbin.mobbin.search_screens`, and the TypeScript callable is `mobbin.mobbin_search_screens(args)`.
116: > The call below uses the confirmed form. Live RESPONSE behavior remains unexercised because authenticated calls await operator OAuth. Re-confirm the name with `tool_info` in each session.

118: Mandatory discovery-first sequence: `list_tools()` or `search_tools({ task_description: "Mobbin screen design research", limit: 10 })` -> filter to the `mobbin` manual -> `tool_info()` on the exact dotted name -> only then `call_tool_chain({ code })`. Cite every selected reference by its `mobbin_url`.

120: ```typescript
121: call_tool_chain({
122:   code: `
123:     const result = await mobbin.mobbin_search_screens({
124:       query: "iOS banking app onboarding identity verification",
125:       platform: "ios",
126:       limit: 5
127:     });
128:     return { success: true, data: result, errors: [], timestamp: new Date().toISOString() };
129:   `
130: });

133: ### Research workflows (query intents over the three live tools)
134: 
135: App, screen, and element research remain intent-specific query designs over `search_screens`; flow and website-section research now have dedicated live-discovered tools (2026-07-16):
136: 
137: 1. **App research** — name the app/company/category and comparison goal ("banking apps onboarding identity verification"); compare `app_name`, platform, structure, visible patterns.
138: 2. **Screen research** — name the concrete screen/state/job ("iOS subscription cancellation confirmation", "web empty-state dashboard"); start at 5 results; cite each `mobbin_url` used.
139: 3. **Flow research** — use `search_flows`: describe one user journey ("onboarding with personalization steps"); it returns ordered flow objects (`screens[].position`, `actions[]`, `screen_count`), superseding the old screens-only reconstruction guidance. Label anything beyond the returned ordering as inference.
140: 4. **Element research** — name component + context/state ("bottom-sheet destructive confirmation", "inline validation on signup"); analyze element behavior within returned screens; never fabricate an element-detail tool.
141: 5. **Website-section research** — use `search_sections`: describe one section ("pricing page with plan comparison table"); results carry `site_name` and section images.

143: Official skill operating sequence:
144: 1. Derive query terms from the user's actual words.
145: 2. Infer `ios` or `web` from app context. If unclear, ask.
146: 3. Announce a short search plan.
147: 4. Call `search_screens` in the same turn.
148: 5. Visually inspect returned references for content, structure, styling and interaction. Compare repeats and meaningful differences, then synthesize principles.
149: 6. Answer from evidence tied to returned screens.

151: The official skill's optional evidence-board writer is **excluded** from this transport because the transport has a read-only boundary.
152: 
153: Context discipline: start `limit: 5`; ask before widening materially (do not exceed ~15 just for variety); report `failed[]` entries and missing images as partial success, never silently discard; retain `mobbin_url` as provenance for every selected reference.

155: ### Auth, plans, and limits
156: 
157: - **Auth**: Browser OAuth is the only auth method: protected-resource discovery, Dynamic Client Registration (RFC 7591), authorization-code + PKCE S256 and `openid` scope.
158:   - **No static Mobbin API key exists for MCP.** The API-key Bearer model belongs to the separate Team/Enterprise REST API. Never conflate the two.
159:   - Client access is revocable from Mobbin Account Settings -> MCP.
160:   - Adapter auth state persists under `~/.mcp-auth` (or `MCP_REMOTE_CONFIG_DIR`) and is **operator-owned**. Never inspect, clear or repair it.
161:   - A live unauthenticated probe returned HTTP 401 with a `WWW-Authenticate` pointer to the protected-resource metadata. A pre-authorization 401 is the **expected** challenge, not a missing-key error.
162:   - End-to-end OAuth through the local Code Mode + `mcp-remote` bridge is **Inferred**, not verified. No operator has completed the flow in this repo's record.
163: - **Plans**: MCP is available on **Pro, Team and Enterprise**; Free is excluded. State "MCP starts at Pro".
164:   - The exact Free denial status/payload/UX is UNVERIFIED. Do not guess failure semantics.
165:   - No reviewed source documents different MCP tool sets per paid tier. Do not invent per-tool tier gates.
166:   - Per-plan usage caps within eligible tiers are undocumented. Finance+ is a separate paid add-on, and its MCP result coverage is unestablished.
167: - **Rate limit**: **60 requests per 60 seconds per user**; on 429 honor `Retry-After`, then exponential backoff with jitter.
168: - **Transport**: the provider itself is a hosted remote server over **Streamable HTTP** at `https://api.mobbin.com/mcp` — there is no local package to install; the official repo is metadata-only. The local bridge is `npx -y mcp-remote` over stdio (HTTP-first, SSE fallback only on HTTP 404; experimental, externally versioned; Node 18+ and working `npx` are prerequisites).

28: ## 1. WHEN TO USE
29: 
30: ### Activation Triggers
31: 
32: **Use when** the user wants to:
33: - Search Mobbin for real-app design references: screens for a UI pattern or state, apps for category comparison, flows for journey steps, or elements for component behavior in context.
34: - Find screen examples from shipped apps ("show me iOS banking onboarding screens", "web empty-state dashboard examples").
35: - Research how real products handle a flow or journey through screen evidence ("first-run onboarding progression", "forgot-password recovery").
36: - Wire, verify, or troubleshoot the registered `mobbin` Code Mode manual, its OAuth authentication, its plan gating, or its rate limit.
37: 
38: **Keyword Triggers**: "mobbin", "mobbin mcp", "app design research", "screen examples", "ux flow references", "real app screenshots", "search mobbin".
39: 
40: ### Use Cases
41: 
42: **App research (read-only).** Name the app, company, or category plus the comparison goal ("banking apps onboarding identity verification"); compare `app_name`, platform, structure, and visible patterns across results. Multiple results are evidence, not a design chooser.
43: 
44: **Screen research (read-only).** Name the concrete screen, state, or job ("iOS subscription cancellation confirmation"); start at 5 results; cite each `mobbin_url` used.
45: 
46: **Flow research (read-only).** Describe the journey and target step. The public contract returns screens, not an ordered flow object — reconstruct sequence only when visual evidence supports it, and label the reconstruction as inference.
47: 
48: **Element research (read-only).** Name component plus context/state ("bottom-sheet destructive confirmation", "inline validation on signup"); analyze element behavior within returned screens.
49: 
50: **Wiring and auth verification.** Report the manual's registration state honestly (presence is the healthy result; absence is a failure symptom to escalate), explain the OAuth-only model and plan gate, and never repair auth state yourself.

52: ### When NOT to Use
53: 
54: **Skip this skill when:**
55: - The work is measured design-reference extraction: turning a live website's real CSS into a Style Reference DESIGN.md of named design tokens (type scale, components, Quick-Start CSS/Tailwind). That is `sk-design-md-generator`; this packet only retrieves Mobbin screenshot evidence.
56: - The task is styles, screens, or flows research through Refero. That is `mcp-refero`, the sibling transport.
57: - The task is Figma work (inspect, tokens, render, Code Connect). That is `mcp-figma`.
58: - The task is browser automation, live-page inspection, or visual preview of a built page. That is `mcp-chrome-devtools`.
59: - The work is generic app coding with no design-reference input: use `sk-code`.
60: - The target is Mobbin's documentation search. `docs.mobbin.com/mcp` is a **separate** Mintlify docs-search MCP, not the design-reference server; this packet targets `api.mobbin.com/mcp` only.
61: - The user asks to change this repo's files, edit the registered `.utcp_config.json` manual, or repair auth state. This transport forbids Write/Edit/Task, never mutates the workspace, and the registered manual is operator-owned.

155: ### Auth, plans, and limits
156: 
157: - **Auth**: Browser OAuth is the only auth method: protected-resource discovery, Dynamic Client Registration (RFC 7591), authorization-code + PKCE S256 and `openid` scope.
158:   - **No static Mobbin API key exists for MCP.** The API-key Bearer model belongs to the separate Team/Enterprise REST API. Never conflate the two.
159:   - Client access is revocable from Mobbin Account Settings -> MCP.
160:   - Adapter auth state persists under `~/.mcp-auth` (or `MCP_REMOTE_CONFIG_DIR`) and is **operator-owned**. Never inspect, clear or repair it.
161:   - A live unauthenticated probe returned HTTP 401 with a `WWW-Authenticate` pointer to the protected-resource metadata. A pre-authorization 401 is the **expected** challenge, not a missing-key error.
162:   - End-to-end OAuth through the local Code Mode + `mcp-remote` bridge is **Inferred**, not verified. No operator has completed the flow in this repo's record.
163: - **Plans**: MCP is available on **Pro, Team and Enterprise**; Free is excluded. State "MCP starts at Pro".
164:   - The exact Free denial status/payload/UX is UNVERIFIED. Do not guess failure semantics.
165:   - No reviewed source documents different MCP tool sets per paid tier. Do not invent per-tool tier gates.
166:   - Per-plan usage caps within eligible tiers are undocumented. Finance+ is a separate paid add-on, and its MCP result coverage is unestablished.
167: - **Rate limit**: **60 requests per 60 seconds per user**; on 429 honor `Retry-After`, then exponential backoff with jitter.
168: - **Transport**: the provider itself is a hosted remote server over **Streamable HTTP** at `https://api.mobbin.com/mcp` — there is no local package to install; the official repo is metadata-only. The local bridge is `npx -y mcp-remote` over stdio (HTTP-first, SSE fallback only on HTTP 404; experimental, externally versioned; Node 18+ and working `npx` are prerequisites).

19: ## 1. OVERVIEW

21: ### Purpose
22: 
23: The live contract for the Mobbin MCP. **Live Code Mode discovery ran 2026-07-16, pre-auth** (fixture: [`discovery-fixture-2026-07-16.json`](./discovery-fixture-2026-07-16.json)), and it **SUPERSEDES the research's one-public-tool baseline**:

There are still no `search_apps`, `search_elements`, detail, image-download, or mutation tools, and none may be invented beyond the discovered inventory.

41: ## 2. THE LIVE-DISCOVERED TOOLS (THREE)
42: 
43: Live-listed pre-auth on 2026-07-16 ([`discovery-fixture-2026-07-16.json`](./discovery-fixture-2026-07-16.json)); all schemas below are the fixture's declared TypeScript interfaces. **[CONFIRMED: fixture]**
44: 
45: | Tool | Posture | Required inputs | Optional inputs | Declared output |
46: |---|---|---|---|---|
47: | `search_screens` | Read/search | `query`: natural language; `platform`: `"ios" \| "web"` | `mode?: "deep" \| "standard" \| "fast"`; `limit?`; `exclude_screen_ids?: string[]`; `image_format?: "webp" \| "jpg"` | `{ query, screens: [{ id, image_url, mobbin_url, app_name, platform }] }` |
48: | `search_flows` | Read/search | `query`: one user journey; `platform`: `"ios" \| "web"` | `limit?`; `page?` (max 20); `image_format?` | `{ query, page, has_next_page, flows: [{ id, name, actions[], mobbin_url, app_name, platform, screen_count, screens: [{ screen_id, image_url, position }] }] }` |
49: | `search_sections` | Read/search | `query`: one website section | `limit?`; `page?`; `image_format?` | `{ query, page, has_next_page, sections: [{ id, image_url, mobbin_url, site_name }] }` |
50: 
51: `search_flows` and `search_sections` **supersede the research's one-public-tool baseline** (dated 2026-07-16): the official `mobbin-search` skill documented only `search_screens`; the live registry lists all three.
52: 
53: Inline images: all three tool descriptions instruct examining returned images and citing `mobbin_url` links. Note the fixture's declared `search_screens` output is `{ query, screens[] }` — the research-documented `index` and `failed[]` fields do **not** appear in the declared schema; verify their presence or absence on the first authenticated call rather than assuming either shape. **[CONFIRMED: fixture schema; live response shape untested]**
54: 
55: ### Hard constraints
56: 
57: - `query` is natural language, derived from the user's actual words; one screen/journey/section per query (the fixture descriptions forbid combined intents, negations, and vague style words). Do not put platform words in `query` — use the `platform` parameter.
58: - `platform` is the enum `"ios" | "web"` on `search_screens` and `search_flows`; infer from app context, ask when unclear. `search_sections` has no platform parameter. **[CONFIRMED: fixture]**
59: - `limit` guidance: higher limits increase context usage (fixture wording); the official guidance treats ~15 as the ceiling for variety. Start small; ask before widening materially.
60: - Missing images or partial results are **partial success**: report them, never silently discard.
61: - Preserve unknown response fields untouched; declared schemas are discovery output, and live calls remain unexercised.
62: - Cite every selected reference by its `mobbin_url` (provenance).
63: 
64: ### The `deep` mode (RESOLVED 2026-07-16)
65: 
66: The research record's input-vs-server-behavior conflict is **resolved by the fixture schema**: search mode is a client-settable input on `search_screens` — `mode?: "deep" | "standard" | "fast"`, where `"standard"` returns results with low latency, `"deep"` uses an AI-powered pipeline that interprets intent and scores results for relevance (for nuanced queries), and `"fast"` is a deprecated alias for `"standard"` slated for removal. **[CONFIRMED: fixture `search_screens` schema]**
67: 
68: ### Completeness boundary
69:

Mutation-refusal check: passed (no mutation-capable tool listed). **[CONFIRMED: fixture]**
72: - **Not allowed**: inventing `search_apps`, `search_elements`, detail/image/mutation tools, or anything beyond the discovered inventory.
73: - The packet's read-only guarantee is an **authorization boundary**: allow only verified read/search tools; if live discovery ever returns a mutation-capable tool, refuse it and require an explicit reviewed contract change.
74: 
75: ### Two-server disambiguation
76: 
77: `docs.mobbin.com/mcp` is a **separate** Mintlify docs-search MCP ("Mobbin Docs") exposing `search_mobbin_docs`, `query_docs_filesystem_mobbin_docs`, and `submit_feedback`. It belongs to the docs server, not the design server. This packet targets `api.mobbin.com/mcp` only. **[CONFIRMED]**
78:

81: ## 3. THE QUERY-INTENT WORKFLOWS
82: 
83: App, screen, and element research run over `search_screens`; flow research now has a dedicated tool:
84: 
85: 1. **App research** — name the app/company/category and the comparison goal ("banking apps onboarding identity verification"); compare `app_name`, platform, structure, and visible patterns across results. Multiple results are evidence, not a design chooser.
86: 2. **Screen research** — name the concrete screen/state/job ("iOS subscription cancellation confirmation", "web empty-state dashboard"); start at 5 results; cite each `mobbin_url` used.
87: 3. **Flow research** — use `search_flows` (live-discovered 2026-07-16): describe one user journey ("onboarding with personalization steps", "checkout with payment method selection"); it returns flow objects with ordered per-screen previews (`screens[].position`), `actions[]`, and `screen_count` — a real sequence contract, superseding the old screens-only reconstruction guidance. Reconstruction-as-inference labeling still applies to anything beyond the returned ordering.
88: 4. **Element research** — name component + context/state ("bottom-sheet destructive confirmation", "inline validation on signup"); analyze element behavior within returned screens; never fabricate an element-detail tool.
89: 5. **Website-section research** — use `search_sections` (live-discovered 2026-07-16): describe one section ("pricing page with plan comparison table", "hero section with signup form"); results carry `site_name` and section images.
90: 
91: ### The official operating sequence
92: 
93: From the official `mobbin-search` skill: derive query terms from the user's actual words -> infer `ios` vs `web` from app context (unclear -> ask) -> announce a short search plan -> call `search_screens` in the same turn -> visually inspect returned references (observe content, structure, styling, interaction; compare repeats and meaningful differences; synthesize principles) -> answer from evidence tied to returned screens.
94: 
95: The official skill's **optional evidence-board writer is excluded** from this transport: board creation violates the non-mutating packet boundary.
96: 
97: ### The local transport boundary
98: 
99: This transport allows breadth while researching (multiple apps, screens, intents compared through metadata and images), but it produces no design tokens or Style Reference of its own: a measured Style Reference of real, extracted design tokens is `sk-design-md-generator`'s output, produced from a live site's CSS. A transport response is untrusted reference evidence, never a measured token set. Search rank is not a verdict; an appealing screenshot is not an extracted token; and no design-token set or Style Reference ever comes from this packet.

104: 
105: | Surface | Free | Pro | Team | Enterprise | Credential |
106: |---------|:----:|:---:|:----:|:----------:|------------|

108: | Mobbin MCP | **No** | **Yes** | **Yes** | **Yes** | Browser OAuth |

111: **[CONFIRMED: docs.mobbin.com/mcp/introduction, /overview, /api/quickstart, mobbin.com/pricing]**
112: 
113: - No reviewed source documents different MCP tool sets per paid tier — do not invent per-tool tier gates.
114: - The exact Free-account MCP denial behavior (status/payload/UX) is **UNVERIFIED** — state "MCP starts at Pro" without guessing failure semantics.

117: - The separate REST API (Team/Enterprise, workspace Bearer key, e.g. `POST /v1/screens/search`) must never be conflated with MCP.

119: **Rate limit** **[CONFIRMED: docs.mobbin.com/rate-limits]**: 60 requests per 60 seconds per user. On 429, honor `Retry-After`, then exponential backoff with jitter. Do not invent finer-grained burst or concurrency contracts.

125: `github.com/mobbin/skills` (MIT) is the official skills repository. Its `skills/` tree contains **exactly one skill: `mobbin-search`**, whose SKILL.md is the authoritative usage contract for `search_screens` (inputs, response shape, workflow, visual-analysis guidance, optional board path). 43: Live-listed pre-auth on 2026-07-16 ([`discovery-fixture-2026-07-16.json`](./discovery-fixture-2026-07-16.json)); all schemas below are the fixture's declared TypeScript interfaces. **[CONFIRMED: fixture]**
44: 
45: | Tool | Posture | Required inputs | Optional inputs | Declared output |
46: |---|---|---|---|---|
47: | `search_screens` | Read/search | `query`: natural language; `platform`: `"ios" \| "web"` | `mode?: "deep" \| "standard" \| "fast"`; `limit?`; `exclude_screen_ids?: string[]`; `image_format?: "webp" \| "jpg"` | `{ query, screens: [{ id, image_url, mobbin_url, app_name, platform }] }` |
48: | `search_flows` | Read/search | `query`: one user journey; `platform`: `"ios" \| "web"` | `limit?`; `page?` (max 20); `image_format?` | `{ query, page, has_next_page, flows: [{ id, name, actions[], mobbin_url, app_name, platform, screen_count, screens: [{ screen_id, image_url, position }] }] }` |
49: | `search_sections` | Read/search | `query`: one website section | `limit?`; `page?`; `image_format?` | `{ query, page, has_next_page, sections: [{ id, image_url, mobbin_url, site_name }] }` |
50: 
51: `search_flows` and `search_sections` **supersede the research's one-public-tool baseline** (dated 2026-07-16): the official `mobbin-search` skill documented only `search_screens`; the live registry lists all three.
52: 
53: Inline images: all three tool descriptions instruct examining returned images and citing `mobbin_url` links. Note the fixture's declared `search_screens` output is `{ query, screens[] }` — the research-documented `index` and `failed[]` fields do **not** appear in the declared schema; verify their presence or absence on the first authenticated call rather than assuming either shape. **[CONFIRMED: fixture schema; live response shape untested]**
54: 
55: ### Hard constraints
56: 
57: - `query` is natural language, derived from the user's actual words; one screen/journey/section per query (the fixture descriptions forbid combined intents, negations, and vague style words). Do not put platform words in `query` — use the `platform` parameter.
58: - `platform` is the enum `"ios" | "web"` on `search_screens` and `search_flows`; infer from app context, ask when unclear. `search_sections` has no platform parameter. **[CONFIRMED: fixture]**
59: - `limit` guidance: higher limits increase context usage (fixture wording); the official guidance treats ~15 as the ceiling for variety. Start small; ask before widening materially.
60: - Missing images or partial results are **partial success**: report them, never silently discard.
61: - Preserve unknown response fields untouched; declared schemas are discovery output, and live calls remain unexercised.
62: - Cite every selected reference by its `mobbin_url` (provenance).
63: 
64: ### The `deep` mode (RESOLVED 2026-07-16)
65: 
66: The research record's input-vs-server-behavior conflict is **resolved by the fixture schema**: search mode is a client-settable input on `search_screens` — `mode?: "deep" | "standard" | "fast"`, where `"standard"` returns results with low latency, `"deep"` uses an AI-powered pipeline that interprets intent and scores results for relevance (for nuanced queries), and `"fast"` is a deprecated alias for `"standard"` slated for removal. **[CONFIRMED: fixture `search_screens` schema]**
67: 
68: ### Completeness boundary
69: 
70: - **Documented baseline (historical)**: `search_screens` was the only publicly documented tool — the official `skills/` tree contains exactly one skill (`mobbin-search`) naming only `search_screens`. **[CONFIRMED at 2026-07-16: server repo HEAD `bbee2a6be34d251c580ba80bb8b407c87587aba7` (2026-06-03); skills repo HEAD `9657786338c5e7fed597031982398a8d99681fec` (2026-05-04)]**
71: - **Live inventory (supersedes the baseline)**: pre-auth `list_tools` on 2026-07-16 returned exactly three `mobbin.*` entries — `search_screens`, `search_flows`, `search_sections` — all read-only search tools. Mutation-refusal check: passed (no mutation-capable tool listed). **[CONFIRMED: fixture]**
72: - **Not allowed**: inventing `search_apps`, `search_elements`, detail/image/mutation tools, or anything beyond the discovered inventory.
73: - The packet's read-only guarantee is an **authorization boundary**: allow only verified read/search tools; if live discovery ever returns a mutation-capable tool, refuse it and require an explicit reviewed contract change.
74: 
75: ### Two-server disambiguation
76: 
77: `docs.mobbin.com/mcp` is a **separate** Mintlify docs-search MCP ("Mobbin Docs") exposing `search_mobbin_docs`, `query_docs_filesystem_mobbin_docs`, and `submit_feedback`. It belongs to the docs server, not the design server. This packet targets `api.mobbin.com/mcp` only. **[CONFIRMED]**
78: 
79: ---
80: 
81: ## 3. THE QUERY-INTENT WORKFLOWS
82: 
83: App, screen, and element research run over `search_screens`; flow research now has a dedicated tool:
84: 
85: 1. **App research** — name the app/company/category and the comparison goal ("banking apps onboarding identity verification"); compare `app_name`, platform, structure, and visible patterns across results. Multiple results are evidence, not a design chooser.
86: 2. **Screen research** — name the concrete screen/state/job ("iOS subscription cancellation confirmation", "web empty-state dashboard"); start at 5 results; cite each `mobbin_url` used.
87: 3. **Flow research** — use `search_flows` (live-discovered 2026-07-16): describe one user journey ("onboarding with personalization steps", "checkout with payment method selection"); it returns flow objects with ordered per-screen previews (`screens[].position`), `actions[]`, and `screen_count` — a real sequence contract, superseding the old screens-only reconstruction guidance. Reconstruction-as-inference labeling still applies to anything beyond the returned ordering.
88: 4. **Element research** — name component + context/state ("bottom-sheet destructive confirmation", "inline validation on signup"); analyze element behavior within returned screens; never fabricate an element-detail tool.
89: 5. **Website-section research** — use `search_sections` (live-discovered 2026-07-16): describe one section ("pricing page with plan comparison table", "hero section with signup form"); results carry `site_name` and section images.
90: 
91: ### The official operating sequence
92: 
93: From the official `mobbin-search` skill: derive query terms from the user's actual words -> infer `ios` vs `web` from app context (unclear -> ask) -> announce a short search plan -> call `search_screens` in the same turn -> visually inspect returned references (observe content, structure, styling, interaction; compare repeats and meaningful differences; synthesize principles) -> answer from evidence tied to returned screens.
94: 
95: The official skill's **optional evidence-board writer is excluded** from this transport: board creation violates the non-mutating packet boundary.
96: 
97: ### The local transport boundary
98: 
99: This transport allows breadth while researching (multiple apps, screens, intents compared through metadata and images), but it produces no design tokens or Style Reference of its own: a measured Style Reference of real, extracted design tokens is `sk-design-md-generator`'s output, produced from a live site's CSS. A transport response is untrusted reference evidence, never a measured token set. Search rank is not a verdict; an appealing screenshot is not an extracted token; and no design-token set or Style Reference ever comes from this packet.
100: 
101: ---
102: 
103: ## 4. PLAN GATING AND LIMITS
104: 
105: | Surface | Free | Pro | Team | Enterprise | Credential |
106: |---------|:----:|:---:|:----:|:----------:|------------|
107: | Mobbin website | Limited browsing | Full | Included | Included | User session |
108: | Mobbin MCP | **No** | **Yes** | **Yes** | **Yes** | Browser OAuth |
109: | Mobbin REST API | No | No | Yes | Yes | Workspace API key |
110: 
111: **[CONFIRMED: docs.mobbin.com/mcp/introduction, /overview, /api/quickstart, mobbin.com/pricing]**
112: 
113: - No reviewed source documents different MCP tool sets per paid tier — do not invent per-tool tier gates.
114: - The exact Free-account MCP denial behavior (status/payload/UX) is **UNVERIFIED** — state "MCP starts at Pro" without guessing failure semantics.
115: - Per-plan usage caps within eligible tiers (searches/day, screens/query, whether the ~15 `limit` ceiling is plan-derived) are **undocumented** — carry as a caveat, never a claimed matrix.
116: - Finance+ is a separate paid add-on; whether it changes MCP-returned datasets is **unestablished**.
117: - The separate REST API (Team/Enterprise, workspace Bearer key, e.g. `POST /v1/screens/search`) must never be conflated with MCP.
118: 
119: **Rate limit** **[CONFIRMED: docs.mobbin.com/rate-limits]**: 60 requests per 60 seconds per user. On 429, honor `Retry-After`, then exponential backoff with jitter. Do not invent finer-grained burst or concurrency contracts.
120: 
121: ---
122: 
123: ## 5. THE OFFICIAL SKILLS REPOSITORY
124: 
125: `github.com/mobbin/skills` (MIT) is the official skills repository. Its `skills/` tree contains **exactly one skill: `mobbin-search`**, whose SKILL.md is the authoritative usage contract for `search_screens` (inputs, response shape, workflow, visual-analysis guidance, optional board path). The documented install path for clients that want the skill bundle is `npx skills add mobbin/skills` (plus a manual clone/copy path) — this installs **guidance only** and does not replace the MCP manual or OAuth setup. This packet references the repository and deliberately does not vendor it.
